alignments.note: Preposition to unto; English puts the phrase after the verb (rule 25).
Construct noun with the supplied the, the rectum being an anarthrous proper name (rule 29).
Nomen rectum takes the relational of (rule 19), headed on the name.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary (rule 17), headed on the lexical verb.
The לְ of לֵאמֹר has no English realization (rule 27).

The contiguous casuistic formula אִישׁ אִישׁ כִּי is rendered by the single word Whosoever, so rule 30's one-English-word condition is met and the whole expression is one unit headed on the morpheme carrying the lexeme, rather than two rendered morphemes beside a כִּי marked unrepresented. Whosoever carries the relative subordination כִּי supplies as well as the distributive any man, so rule 22's unrendered-occurrence sentence does not reach that particle. The competing reading gives Whosoever to the doubled אִישׁ alone and leaves כִּי unrepresented.
The ASV writes no connective for the apodosis waw (rule 14).

review_notes: Corrected: כִּי joins the אִישׁ אִישׁ fusion instead of standing as an unrepresented unit. Rule 30 states that where one English word renders a multi-word Hebrew expression the whole expression is one unit headed on the lexeme-bearing morpheme, rather than one rendered morpheme beside others marked unrepresented, and the three morphemes are contiguous, so the contiguity condition is met.
The relative force of Whosoever is what כִּי contributes — any man (אִישׁ אִישׁ) plus who (כִּי) — so rule 22's first sentence, which governs an element the ASV has left unwritten, does not apply.

This does not disturb the split readings of the same particle elsewhere in the chapter, where the ASV writes a separate English word for it (that at v.17, if at v.19); there the one-English-word condition is unmet and rule 2 splits.
